titel: Vehicle, load, trailer and the environment
intro: This unit is about the car itself and about what you carry with it. You learn which requirements your vehicle has to meet, when it gets tested, what you check before you set off and what the lights on your dashboard are telling you. Then comes the load: how long, how wide and how high it may be, what may stick out and when a marker board goes with it. Finally the trailer with its masses and licences, plus the environment: economical driving, the right fuel and the low-emission zone. This is a unit with a lot of numbers in it, so really learn those limits by heart.

U14-P01.titel: Vehicle requirements: what your car has to meet

body.tekst: Your car has to meet a whole series of requirements (voertuigeisen). If something is not in order, you run a bigger risk of an accident and you risk a fine. It is also forbidden to drive a car that is technically in an inadequate state of maintenance.
Below a height of 2 metres, a car may not have sharp parts that could be dangerous to other road users (weggebruikers). The wheels must be properly shielded and all parts must be firmly attached.

Your car runs on pneumatic tyres (luchtbanden) with at least 1.6 mm of tread in the main grooves. The tyres on one axle must have the same size marking, except when you are using an emergency or spare wheel.
The service brake (bedrijfsrem), so your foot brake, must work on all four wheels. The parking brake (parkeerrem), so your handbrake, must work on at least two wheels.

The windscreen (voorruit) and the front side windows must be free of damage and of anything that blocks your view, with working wipers, washers and heating for de-icing and demisting. Film on those windows must let through at least 55% of the light.
You need an interior mirror (binnenspiegel), a left door mirror and a right door mirror, all three without cracks. Equivalent camera monitor systems are allowed too.

All seats lock in every position and all have a seat belt (gordel). You also need a speedometer (snelheidsmeter) that can be read clearly at night, and a horn in good working order with a fixed pitch.

rijen: 2 sidelights, 2 dipped headlights, 2 main-beam headlights, 2 indicators and hazard warning lights
2 tail lights, 3 brake lights, 2 indicators, hazard warning lights, 1 rear fog light, 1 reversing light, number plate lighting and 2 non-triangular retroreflectors

body.tekst: If the fog lights (mistlichten) or the rear fog lights are on, you must be able to see that from a warning light on the dashboard.
A fog light at the front is not compulsory, a rear fog light is. And fitting extra lighting is often not allowed, so find out properly beforehand whether your extra lamps are permitted.

A fire extinguisher, a first aid kit and a warning triangle (gevarendriehoek) are not required by law. They are useful to have with you though: if you come to a stop in a dangerous spot and your hazard lights do not work, you have to put out a warning triangle.
1.6 mm of tread, 55% light transmission, four wheels for the foot brake and two wheels for the handbrake.

U14-P02.titel: The APK test and your check before the drive

body.tekst: Cars, vans, lorries and buses have to be tested regularly. In that general periodic test (algemene periodieke keuring, APK) your vehicle passes if it meets the requirements for road safety and the environment.

Six weeks before the expiry date the RDW sends you a reminder letter. Once it has passed, the test certificate (keuringsbewijs) is valid for 1 or 2 years, and you do not have to be able to show it on the road: the police look it up in a system.

Both the owner or keeper and the driver (bestuurder) are responsible, and so both are punishable if the car is driven without a valid test. The same goes for driving a vehicle that is technically not in order.

rijen: Before the drive, under the bonnet
Oil level, coolant, brake fluid, screen wash and leaks under the car
Mirrors and windows clean and undamaged, lights clean and working, tyres and tyre pressure
Before the drive, in your seat
The setting of your seat, head restraint, steering wheel and mirrors, and your seat belt on
The gauges and lights on your dashboard, and odd noises, vibrations and smells

body.tekst: Pneumatic tyres slowly go down. Check the pressure (bandenspanning) once a month, preferably at the start of the drive while the tyres are still cold. Pressure that is too low gives poorer handling and more fuel consumption.
Tyres filled with nitrogen stay at pressure much longer, because nitrogen does not escape through the pores. You recognise them by a green valve cap.

Make sure your windows and mirrors are clean before you set off. If your windscreen gets dirty on the way, for instance while overtaking (inhalen) a lorry, you have to be able to sort that out straight away with your washer.

items: Park in a safe, level, paved spot
Switch on your hazard lights and put on a high-visibility jacket
Put out the warning triangle if needed
Loosen the wheel nuts by a turn and jack the car up
Take the flat wheel off and fit the spare wheel
Tighten the wheel nuts by hand, lower the car and only then do them up properly

body.tekst: Do not count on a blown bulb always showing up as a message on your dashboard. That is why you check your lights, brake lights and indicators yourself every day.
Tyre pressure once a month, lighting every day.

U14-P03.titel: The dashboard and the driver assistance systems

body.tekst: The middle gauge is the speedometer (snelheidsmeter) and on the left sits the rev counter (toerenteller), which shows how many turns the crankshaft makes per minute. For the exam it is mainly the warning lights (controlelampjes) that count, and there a simple colour rule gets you through almost every question.
If a red warning light comes on, there is a serious fault. Stop in a safe place and switch the engine off so the car can be repaired.
With a yellow warning light you do not have to stop immediately. You can drive on to your dealer, for instance, but do not keep driving any longer than is strictly necessary.
These are the six lights the book points you to. The colour is half the answer: red means stop now, yellow means have it looked at.

rijen: The oil pressure is too low: switch the engine off at once and check the oil level
The coolant is too hot: switch the engine off at once and check the level
The battery is not being charged, the alternator or the V-belt is broken
There is a problem with the braking system
A fault in the engine management system, with consequences for the emissions
The fuel tank is nearly empty

body.tekst: If the coolant light and the battery light come on at the same time, the V-belt has probably snapped. It drives both the coolant pump and the alternator, so your engine will overheat.

The most important rule with driver assistance systems (rijhulpsystemen) is that you as the driver (bestuurder) are always responsible for the driving task yourself. The systems support you, they do not take over the driving. So you also have to know the limits and shortcomings of each system.

items: Emergency braking system (AEB): warns you if you keep too little distance and brakes by itself if you do not act
Speed assistance (ISA): recognises speed limits and warns or brakes if you drive too fast
Blind spot information system (BSM): warns you through your door mirror about vehicles in your blind spot (dode hoek)

body.tekst: The risk of driver assistance systems is that you adjust your behaviour without noticing, for instance driving closer to the car in front because the car will brake anyway. Also make sure your sensors and cameras are clean, because dirt, snow or ice reduces how well they work.
Red means stop, yellow means have it looked at, and the driver always stays responsible.

U14-P04.titel: Load: height, width and what sticks out

body.tekst: A car may be at most 12 metres long, at most 2.55 metres wide and at most 4 metres high, the last two including the load (lading). The same three dimensions apply to a trailer (aanhangwagen).
A combination of car and trailer may be at most 18 metres long, even though each part on its own may be 12 metres.

A load on a roof rack (imperiaal) or on a carrier on your towbar may stick out at most 20 cm beyond your car on each side. Do not go over the permitted roof load, and only use a carrier for what it is meant for.

rijen: Max. 1 metre behind the car and max. 5 metres behind the rear axle
Max. 1 metre in front of the car
Max. 1 metre behind the trailer and max. 5 metres behind the rear axle
Max. half the length of the trailer, up to max. 5 metres behind the rear axle

body.tekst: On a trailer, a divisible load may stick out at the sides up to a total width of 2.55 metres. An indivisible load there may be at most 3 metres wide.
On a car, marker boards (markeringsborden) for a protruding load are not compulsory. On a trailer they are: if the load sticks out more than 10 cm at a side, or more than 1 metre at the rear.
A marker board for a protruding load has diagonal red and white stripes. You fit width marking at the front as well as at the rear, and at night the boards have to be lit.
Spread your load well. If your car hangs backwards, your headlights shine upwards and you dazzle oncoming drivers. Secure the load too, so that it stays in place when you brake or swerve.
A divisible load may never stick out at the front; an indivisible one may do so on the car, up to 1 metre.

U14-P05.titel: The trailer and your driving licence

body.tekst: The law calls a trailer (aanhangwagen) a vehicle that is clearly meant to be moved along by a motor vehicle. Semi-trailers, caravans and a car being towed fall under it too.

If a trailer has no registration certificate (kentekenbewijs), the permitted maximum mass (toegestane maximummassa) is 750 kg. Up to and including 750 kg it carries a white number plate with the registration of the towing car; above 750 kg the trailer has its own registration certificate and a yellow plate with its own registration.
A trailer up to and including 1,500 kg has to have a breakaway brake (losbreekreminrichting) or a safety coupling (hulpkoppeling). Above 1,500 kg a breakaway brake is compulsory.

A braking system is not compulsory if the total mass of the trailer is less than 750 kg and less than 50% of the kerb weight (rijklaargewicht) of the towing vehicle. In all other cases it is compulsory.

The load under the coupling of a centre-axle trailer (middenasaanhangwagen) up to 750 kg has to point downwards and may be at most 50 kg. If the trailer weighs more than 750 kg, that load may not be less than 1% of the permitted maximum mass.

rijen: More than 4,250 kg, up to 7,000 kg

body.tekst: You may not carry people on or in a trailer or caravan. If the trailer gets in the way of your view to the rear, you have to fit extra door mirrors on your car.

Every trailer and semi-trailer has two triangular retroreflectors at the rear. If you see those from behind, you know you are coming up on a vehicle combination. That is useful to know before you start overtaking (inhalen).
If this sign stands at a road, that road is closed to motor vehicles with a trailer. You see it at a narrow street or a tight bridge, for instance, where you cannot get through with a combination.
With a BE licence you may also drive where B with code 96 is needed, but it does not work the other way round. The practical tests for both are the same, so almost everyone goes for BE.
750 kg is the first limit, 3,500 kg the second and 4,250 kg the limit above which only BE still counts.

U14-P06.titel: Environment: economical driving, refuelling and the low-emission zone

body.tekst: The emissions from combustion engines add to global warming and to an unhealthy living environment. While driving on electricity or hydrogen, no harmful substances are released.

Cars are required to be fitted with a catalytic converter (katalysator). It turns 90% of the harmful exhaust gases into harmless substances, but only works properly once the engine is up to temperature, after 10 to 15 minutes of driving.

items: Drive off gently straight after starting, in winter too
Use the rev counter to change up in good time
Keep your distance and look ahead, so that you do not have to brake all the time
Let your car roll out in gear when you have to stop
Switch the engine off if you have to stand still for longer than 1 minute
Use your air conditioning sparingly: with the air conditioning on, consumption can be up to 15% higher

body.tekst: Make sure you know which fuel belongs in your car; it is on the fuel flap or in the handbook. On the nozzle there is a code that tells you the type of fuel.
If you have put in the wrong fuel anyway, do not start the engine. Parts of your engine and fuel system can be badly damaged. Call in expert help to have your fuel system drained.

Noise nuisance is a form of pollution too. Fitting a noisy exhaust, playing music at full blast, sounding your horn unnecessarily, playing with your accelerator and pulling away with squealing tyres are therefore forbidden.

A low-emission zone (milieuzone) is an area that is closed to cars, vans, lorries or buses with a diesel engine. A zero-emission zone (nul-emissiezone) is closed to all sorts of vans and lorries, except for zero-emission vehicles running on electricity or hydrogen.

This round sign stands in a ZONE frame at the start of a low-emission zone or a zero-emission zone. Sub-plates (onderborden) tell you which vehicles and which emission classes the zone applies to; your own emission class is on the registration certificate.

items: The rolling resistance and the fuel consumption
The grip on a wet road surface and the braking distance (remweg)
The noise produced at 80 km/h
The performance in heavy snow or ice

body.tekst: Think about cleaning and maintenance too. Make sure no polluting or dangerous substances end up in the soil or the drains, and take old parts, batteries and tyres to the right collection point. In many municipalities washing your car on the public road is forbidden, by the way.
Which fuel belongs in your car
The shape tells you in one look which sort you are dealing with, even in a country where you cannot read the words on the pump. Round is petrol, square is diesel and a diamond is gas.

Petrol in a modern diesel car damages the fuel system while you drive, because petrol is less greasy than diesel. Diesel in a petrol engine burns far less well, so the engine runs badly or is damaged.
The catalytic converter and the soot filter

items: Avoid long attempts at starting
Do not push or tow the car while the engine is still warm
Never switch off the ignition while the car is moving
Never run the fuel tank completely empty

body.tekst: Like the rest of the exhaust, the catalytic converter gets very hot. So do not park your car above dry leaves or withered grass.
Besides the catalytic converter, a diesel car also has a soot filter (roetfilter) in the exhaust system. It filters out the small soot particles, because those cause cancer.

With a diesel engine the catalytic converter sometimes uses the additive AdBlue to clean the exhaust gases. The car then has a separate tank for it with a blue cap, and a light on the dashboard tells you when to top it up.
Go to the garage for a technical check straight away if your fuel consumption goes up, if the engine runs unevenly, or if dark smoke comes out of the exhaust.
A low-emission zone looks at diesel and emission class, a zero-emission zone only lets zero-emission vehicles in.

U14-P07.titel: Driver assistance: what a new car must have

body.tekst: Driver assistance systems are known together as ADAS. On the previous page you read the main rule: they support you and do not take over the driving. Here is which systems a new car carries these days and what they do.
Switch a driver assistance system on or off when the situation calls for it. In doing so you look at four factors: the road, the weather, the traffic and your own condition as a driver.
What a new car must have

rijen: Detects people and objects behind the car and warns you with a sound
Warns you on the dashboard if the pressure in one or more tyres is too low
Warns you if a collision threatens with pedestrians or cyclists in front of your car
Watches your eye direction and head position with cameras and warns you if you are distracted
Warns you if you keep too little distance and brakes by itself if you do not act
Records your driving behaviour before, during and after a collision
Warns you through your door mirror about vehicles in the blind spot beside and behind you
Recognises speed limits and warns or brakes if you go too fast
Makes your rear lights flash to warn the cars behind you when you brake hard
Makes an alcohol interlock simple to install
Steers back if your car is about to leave its lane
Spots sleepiness or slipping attention from your driving and steering pattern

body.tekst: Two things the exam likes to ask. Lane keeping assistance does not step in when you have indicated, because then you are leaving the lane on purpose. And you may switch speed assistance off, but it is automatically back on at the start of every new trip.
Systems that can come on top

rijen: Keeps the following distance you set and adjusts your speed to the traffic
Switches between main beam and dipped beam by itself, based on other traffic
Steers for you while parking, while you work the accelerator and the brake
Warns you when a door is opened if a cyclist or vehicle is coming
Warns you when reversing about crossing traffic coming from the side
Warns you about oncoming traffic when you turn left
Holds the car still in a queue or at a traffic light without you holding the brake
Recognises road signs and shows them on your dashboard, often together with ISA

body.tekst: You do not have to know every abbreviation by heart, but you do have to know what a system does and where it stops. Every system has limits and cannot step in in every situation.
A driver assistance system warns or helps, you keep driving. On or off depends on the road, the weather, the traffic and yourself.
